clues: An observatory commissioned by a king in 1675 stands on a hill in a park, overlooking a river to the north.
In 1884 a conference in Washington chose the meridian passing through it as the prime meridian for the whole world, and it gave its name to a time standard.

reveal.explanation: The Royal Observatory, Greenwich, is situated on a hill in Greenwich Park in south-east London, overlooking the River Thames to the north. It was commissioned in 1675 by King Charles II. In 1884 the International Meridian Conference in Washington decided that the Greenwich meridian should be the prime meridian for the whole world, and the observatory gave its name to Greenwich Mean Time.

sources.excerpt: The Royal Observatory, Greenwich (51°28′37″N 0°00′53″W) is an observatory situated on a hill in Greenwich Park in south east London, overlooking the River Thames to the north. Because the Prime Meridian passed through it, it gave its name to Greenwich Mean Time. The observatory was commissioned in 1675 by King Charles II. In 1884 the International Meridian Conference in Washington D.C. decided that the Greenwich Prime Meridian should be the Prime meridian for the whole world.
